title: What happens when the context fills up
caption: As the chat fills the window, only the very beginning and the newest stay sharp, the rest blurs, your own first message included, one repeated detail survives, and answers get worse: context rot.

strip.mayFill: <marker>the AI may fill this gap itself</marker>
strip.reason: <marker>Your first message already falls off, and it is one short number among many similar ones</marker>
strip.caveat: <marker>Studies use planted facts, not chat apps</marker>

quality-falls-before-the-limit.description: on a 13-task benchmark almost all of 17 long-context models lost a lot of accuracy as input grew, and only half kept satisfactory performance at 32K tokens although all claimed 32K or more [1].

hsieh-ruler.title: Hsieh et al., RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?

length-alone-hurts.description: even with perfect retrieval, performance dropped by 13.9% to 85% as input grew, and the drop persisted when irrelevant tokens were masked out [1].

du-context-length-alone-hurts.title: Du et al., Context Length Alone Hurts LLM Performance Despite Perfect Retrieval

extra-material-makes-it-worse.description: across 18 models, performance degraded with input length in every experiment, and even a single distractor lowered it [1].

hong-context-rot.title: Hong, Troynikov, Huber, Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance

what-the-studies-measure.description: the studies measure lost accuracy, not a hallucination mechanism [1][2].

mostly-synthetic-tests.description: most studies use a planted fact or padded filler and models of 2024 and 2025, and the size of the drop varies by model and task [1].

du-context-length-alone-hurts.title: Du et al., Context Length Alone Hurts LLM Performance Despite Perfect Retrieval

what-is-context-rot.description: Context rot is the drop in answer quality as the input grows, well before the advertised limit: almost all of 17 long-context models lost a lot of accuracy [1], length alone hurt even with perfect retrieval [2], and across 18 models performance degraded in every experiment [3]. Anthropic explains it as an attention budget that each added token spreads thinner; that is a vendor account, not measured in the studies [4].

only-the-very-start-holds.title: Only the very start holds
only-the-very-start-holds.script: Now watch what happens as this chat grows. Only the very beginning of the window holds the AI's attention: the starting instructions. Your own first message already comes after them, and its attention falls off right away, so being first in the chat is no protection, and you will see why in a moment. One thing before we go on: the numbers on this slide are illustrative, I picked a 200K window and the little bars that show how much the AI looks at each message, to show the shape, not to measure anything.

the-newest-stays-sharp.title: The newest stays sharp
the-newest-stays-sharp.script: The newest stays sharp too. The latest messages are used well, like the last minutes of the call, because they sit right at the end of what the AI is reading.

the-middle-blurs.title: The middle blurs
the-middle-blurs.script: The middle blurs. What you said an hour ago sits in the blurry part, and the AI treats it the way you treat the neighbours' renovation: it was there, but it is thin.

a-standout-survives.title: A standout survives
a-standout-survives.script: And one standout survives. The 60 vegetarian guests, a detail the chat keeps repeating, are still there, and the plan comes back with a vegetarian menu.

answers-get-worse.title: Answers get worse
answers-get-worse.script: Now something new, and this is where it gets uncomfortable. As the chat fills, the answers get worse. This is called context rot.

the-budget-is-forgotten.title: The budget is forgotten
the-budget-is-forgotten.script: Look at the budget. Your very first message said 30,000 euro, and now the plan comes back at 42,300. It was your first message, but only the starting instructions hold the very beginning, so even your first message already falls off. It lost attention by its position, and it is also one short number among many similar ones.

filling-the-gap.title: Filling the gap
filling-the-gap.script: So here is a small number sitting among all the similar numbers from the offers and the searches, and when the AI can't find it, I think it fills the gap itself with something that sounds plausible. I want to be straight about this: that is my hypothesis, not proven.
